graph.title: Arduino Zero Simple Audio Frequency Meter
notes: The parts list is unchanged from step 1.

Breadboard naming follows the catalogue: bank 't' is rows a-e and bank 'b' is rows f-j. In the image the half labelled A-E is the lower half and F-J is the upper half. Only strip membership matters for the circuit.

Rails: top positive is 'tp', bottom negative is 'bn'. The Arduino IOREF pin feeds the top positive rail. The schematic shows IOREF as the supply, so the op-amp runs from the Zero's 3.3 V I/O reference and not 5 V.

The LMV358 straddles the centre gap in columns 14-17. Pin 1 (output) is at 14t.e, 2 (IN-) at 15t.e, 3 (IN+) at 16t.e and 4 (GND) at 17t.e. Pin 8 (V+) is at 14b.f. Pins 5-7 (second amplifier) are unused.

Nets: R8 (r1, 100k) goes from V+ to the non-inverting node, and R9 (r2, 100k) from that node to GND. C1 (c1) joins the jack signal to the same node, which is the op-amp IN+ pin. R10 (r4, 47k) goes from the inverting node to GND. R11 (r3, 47k) goes from the inverting node to the trimmer. The trimmer wiper goes to the op-amp output and A0.

The trimmer is a 10k variable resistor in the feedback path. Its wiper (SIG) goes to the output, one end (VCC port) goes to R11, and the other end (GND port, 1t.e) is left unconnected, as in the schematic. The trimmer's physical hole positions are inferred from the image.

The right end of the short green jumper wire8 is not clearly visible in the image. It is placed at 15t.c, in the strip of op-amp pin 2 (IN-), as the schematic requires, to connect the R10/R11 junction to the inverting input.

The jack uses the audio-jack-35mm card. SLEEVE goes to ground through wire12 and RING1 (the schematic's RIGHT contact) goes to C1 through wire13. TIP, RING2 and the schematic's unused LEFT contact are not wired. The jack wire ends are shown as soldered to the jack board.
The 100 nF capacitor uses the generic two-lead non-polar capacitor type (capacitor-22pf) with value=100nF.
The black ground wire goes to the second GND pin of the power header, next to VIN (GND.2).
